custom_logic_notes: The Directed_Movement_Candle indicator outputs a color code via buffer 4: 0=bearish, 1=neutral, 2=bullish. Long entry requires buffer4[1]==2 (current signal bar bullish) AND buffer4[0]<2 (previous bar was not bullish, i.e. a transition). Short entry requires buffer4[1]==0 (current signal bar bearish) AND buffer4[0]>0 (previous bar was not bearish, i.e. a transition). This captures directional transitions. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen boolean inputs act as gates to enable/disable long/short entries. BuyPosClose/SellPosClose boolean inputs act as gates for signal-based closing. The EA uses TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose) which contain the actual order logic including position checking. GlobalVariableDel_ cleanup on deinit suggests persistent state management from the trade library. Signal time is set to last bar date + one timeframe period, which likely serves as signal expiration for the trade library.
python_conversion_notes: Must first reimplement the Directed_Movement_Candle custom indicator in Python. This indicator applies RSI with two smoothing passes (first SMA/JJMA pass, second JJMA pass) and outputs a color code (0/1/2) based on level thresholds (70/50/30). The SmoothAlgorithms.mqh library contains 10 smoothing methods (SMA, EMA, SMMA, LWMA, JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) that must be ported - JJMA and JurX are non-trivial recursive algorithms. TradeAlgorithms.mqh must also be ported for BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose logic including signal time expiration. Position sizing depends on MMMode enum (LOT vs PERCENT). SL/TP are in points (1000 and 2000 respectively), which need _Point conversion - no explicit 5-digit adjustment found in code so the trade library may handle it. The new bar check uses CIsNewBar class from the trade library.
